chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-'Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, from Musa ibn Ja'far al-Baghdadi, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from Bundar ibn Hammad, from Abdullah ibn Fadala, from Abu Abdillah or Abu Ja'far (peace be upon both of them). He said: I heard him say:

When a boy reaches three years of age, it is to be said to him seven times: 'Say: There is no god but God.' Then he is left until he reaches three years, seven months, and twenty days, when it is to be said to him seven times: 'Say: Muhammad is the Messenger of God.' Then he is left until he reaches four years. Then it is to be said to him seven times: 'Say: God's blessings be upon Muhammad and his family.' Then he is left until he reaches five years. Then it is to be said to him: 'Which is your right and which is your left?' When he understands that, his face is turned toward the qibla and he is told: Prostrate. Then he is left until he reaches six years. When he reaches six years, he prays and is taught to bow and prostrate. Then he is left until he reaches seven years. When he reaches seven years, he is told: Wash your face and your hands. When he washes them, he is told: Pray. Then he is left until he reaches nine years. When he reaches nine years, he is taught the wudu and made to perform it, and commanded to pray and made to fulfill it. When he has learned the wudu and the prayer, God forgives his parents, God-willing.

key_terms.الغلام: Boy/child — classical Arabic term referring to a male child in early childhood
key_terms.القبلة: The qibla — the direction of prayer, toward the Ka'ba in Mecca
key_terms.الوضوء: Wudu — ritual ablution performed before prayer
key_terms.ضُرب عليه: Made to fulfill/disciplined for it — a technical term indicating enforcement with appropriate mild correction
key_terms.والديه: His parents — the child's learning of prayer benefits them spiritually

ai.seo_question: At what age should children be taught to pray in Islam according to the Imams?
ai.summary: This hadith provides a detailed developmental curriculum for introducing a child to Islam, narrated from one of the Imams (either al-Sadiq or al-Baqir). The instruction begins at age three with the shahada and progresses through the salawat, direction of prayer, and formal worship, culminating at age nine with the full obligation of prayer and ablution. Notably, the teaching emphasizes gradual introduction rather than immediate compulsion, with each milestone reached at a precisely specified age — reflecting the classical Shia jurisprudential principle that religious education should be developmentally appropriate and that a child's learning of prayer benefits the parents spiritually.
